title: Identify the call's job
trigger: A setter, follow-up, or onboarding call is judged as a failed close.
action: Name the intended commitment from the opening and prior context before evaluating missing stages.
suggested_dialogue: The next step here is a conversation with the specialist. Would that be useful?
branches: If the job is booking, assess booking; if closing, assess a buying decision.
practice: State the job and one matching success criterion before scoring.
do_not_apply: Do not invent a call objective from a CRM label alone.

title: Use the existing notes
trigger: The buyer repeats facts already supplied in an application or earlier call.
action: Confirm the relevant prior fact, then ask what changed.
suggested_dialogue: The earlier notes say expansion stalled at hiring. Is that still the issue?
branches: If confirmed, investigate the current gap; if corrected, replace the old note.
practice: Use one verified prior fact without making the buyer retell the whole story.
do_not_apply: Missing notes are unknown context, not proof the rep failed.

title: Repair caller confusion
trigger: The buyer asks who is calling or does not recognize the resource.
action: Restate identity and the actual reason in one sentence before discovery.
suggested_dialogue: This is the team following up on the business guide requested. Does that ring a bell?
branches: If yes, ask permission to continue; if no, explain briefly and offer to end.
practice: The buyer can identify the caller and reason before the next discovery question.
do_not_apply: Never imply a relationship or request that is not supported.

title: Check available attention
trigger: The buyer is driving, distracted, or repeatedly says time is short.
action: Offer a short purposeful conversation or a later time; do not press for detailed figures.
suggested_dialogue: It sounds like now is awkward. Would a better time make this easier?
branches: If available, narrow the agenda; if unavailable, agree a later contact only if wanted.
practice: Ask the availability question and follow the answer.
do_not_apply: Do not infer consent to a long call from answering the phone.

title: Fix connection before diagnosing
trigger: Repeated requests to repeat or statements about cutting out appear.
action: Pause the sales sequence, check whether speech is coming through, and offer a reconnection.
suggested_dialogue: The line keeps cutting out. Should we reconnect, or find another time?
branches: If repaired, recap the last confirmed fact; if not, stop the substantive pitch.
practice: After two explicit hearing problems, address the connection before another sales question.
do_not_apply: Silence after price is not a price objection without a buyer response.

title: Use relevant credibility
trigger: The rep lists company status while the buyer's problem remains unclear.
action: Give only credibility that explains why this conversation is relevant, then return to the buyer.
suggested_dialogue: The team works on this type of bottleneck. Where is it showing up in this business?
branches: If the claim is verified, keep it brief; otherwise omit it.
practice: Each credibility statement connects to a stated buyer problem.
do_not_apply: Company size does not prove this offer fits.

title: Set a useful agenda
trigger: The conversation drifts because neither side knows the intended decision.
action: Explain the sequence and possible next step, including that no fit is possible.
suggested_dialogue: First, clarify the bottleneck. Then check whether the service fits. If it does, discuss the next step.
branches: If the buyer wants a different agenda, agree it; if time is short, reduce scope.
practice: Deliver the agenda in two sentences and get agreement.
do_not_apply: Do not manufacture a promise to buy before discovery.

title: Separate cold from pre-sold
trigger: The buyer already consumed training or had detailed discovery.
action: Ask what is already understood and what still needs resolving.
suggested_dialogue: What is already clear about the service, and what still needs an answer?
branches: If well informed, focus on remaining concerns; if unfamiliar, explain essentials.
practice: Avoid repeating a pitch the buyer can already summarize accurately.
do_not_apply: Do not infer comprehension merely from a sent video link.

title: Prepare for the person
trigger: The rep asks broad questions despite relevant known business context.
action: Review the stated goal, last conversation, and promised follow-up before the call.
suggested_dialogue: Last time the concern was training new hires. What happened with that since then?
branches: If still open, continue there; if resolved, find the current priority.
practice: Write a three-line pre-call brief: goal, open issue, promised next step.
do_not_apply: Research should not become intrusive speculation about private finances.

title: Know the offer before promising
trigger: The rep is uncertain about support, terms, eligibility, or dates.
action: Use an approved offer facts sheet; mark unknowns for confirmation.
suggested_dialogue: That detail needs checking. The confirmed part is [known fact]. Can the team verify the remaining point before a decision?
branches: If verified, answer directly; if unknown, assign an owner and return time.
practice: Separate confirmed facts from assumptions in every proposed script.
do_not_apply: Do not fill missing offer details with the training company's historical terms.

title: Find the reason for the conversation
trigger: The buyer asks for information but no useful objective is known.
action: Ask what the information is meant to help them decide or improve.
suggested_dialogue: What would this information help the business change?
branches: If a specific goal emerges, follow it; if exploratory, offer an appropriate brief overview.
practice: Get a buyer-stated reason without assigning a problem to them.
do_not_apply: Some buyers are legitimately researching.

title: Make the current state concrete
trigger: The rep labels the situation without an example or baseline.
action: Ask what happens today in the part of the business being discussed.
suggested_dialogue: Walk through the last time that happened. What did the team do?
branches: If an example is available, use it; if not, keep the diagnosis tentative.
practice: Capture one observable current-state example.
do_not_apply: Do not demand irrelevant revenue numbers for every sale.

title: Define the desired change
trigger: The buyer says grow, improve, or scale without describing the change.
action: Ask what would be different if the problem were solved.
suggested_dialogue: What would be happening differently three months from now if this worked?
branches: If measurable, record the measure; if qualitative, record the concrete behavior.
practice: Restate the desired result without adding a target the buyer never supplied.
do_not_apply: A desired deadline is not a guaranteed delivery date.

title: Find the obstacle
trigger: Current and desired states are known but the rep jumps to a pitch.
action: Ask what currently prevents the change.
suggested_dialogue: What is stopping the team from doing that now?
branches: If the obstacle is known, test fit; if uncertain, examine a recent example.
practice: Connect the recommendation to a confirmed obstacle.
do_not_apply: Do not presume that taking a call proves the offer is needed.

title: Replace vague labels with an example
trigger: The buyer says systems, people, or strategy and the rep echoes the label.
action: Ask for one incident that shows what the label means in practice.
suggested_dialogue: When the owner is away, what is the first thing that stops working?
branches: If people conflict, explore responsibility; if reporting fails, explore reporting.
practice: Use the example to change the next question.
do_not_apply: Do not repeat the same abstract question louder.

title: Accept a corrected diagnosis
trigger: The buyer corrects the rep's premise and the rep repeats it.
action: Say what changed in the understanding and ask the next question using the correction.
suggested_dialogue: The reports do arrive. The concern is what happens without direct supervision. What breaks first?
branches: If confirmed, investigate execution; if corrected again, let the buyer explain before labeling.
practice: Make the next two questions consistent with the correction.
do_not_apply: A polite yes before a correction does not override the correction.

title: Investigate prior attempts
trigger: A previous provider or internal fix failed.
action: Ask what was tried, for how long, what worked, and what remained missing.
suggested_dialogue: What improved with that approach, and where did it still fall short?
branches: If it worked partly, preserve that gain; if failure cause is unknown, do not diagnose it as fact.
practice: Name the missing component using evidence, not a competitor insult.
do_not_apply: Do not claim every previous provider failed for the same reason.

title: Quantify only with real inputs
trigger: The rep invents the cost of a problem or asserts a huge return.
action: Ask for the buyer's relevant estimate and distinguish it from a measured figure.
suggested_dialogue: Roughly how often does that happen, and what does each instance cost the team?
branches: If reliable figures exist, calculate transparently; if not, use the stated operational impact.
practice: Label every number as measured, estimated, or unknown.
do_not_apply: Do not equate all revenue at risk with profit lost.

title: Recap before the recommendation
trigger: The rep moves from scattered facts to an offer without confirming the problem.
action: Summarize current state, desired change, and obstacle in the buyer's language.
suggested_dialogue: The team can sell, but new hires cannot repeat the process. Is that the main issue to solve?
branches: If yes, map the offer; if no, revise the recap.
practice: The buyer confirms or corrects a concise recap before the pitch.
do_not_apply: Do not force three problems when one clear problem is sufficient.

title: Stop discovery when it is sufficient
trigger: Repeated pain questions add no new information and delay the useful next step.
action: Name what is already understood and ask permission to explain the relevant solution.
suggested_dialogue: The bottleneck is clear enough to discuss an option. Would it help to see how the service addresses it?
branches: If ready, transition; if a material gap remains, ask only that question.
practice: Explain why the next question is necessary or omit it.
do_not_apply: More distress is not the objective of discovery.

title: Build the offer from the problem
trigger: The pitch could be delivered unchanged to any buyer.
action: Connect the confirmed problem to an actual capability and the resulting benefit.
suggested_dialogue: The issue is inconsistent onboarding. [Verified capability] addresses that by [specific mechanism]. Is that the part that matters most?
branches: If relevant, explain the next component; if not, revisit the diagnosis.
practice: Every offered feature has a buyer-specific reason.
do_not_apply: Do not invent a capability to make the mapping work.

title: Explain the result before the mechanics
trigger: The rep lists modules and jargon without explaining their purpose.
action: Describe what the buyer can do differently, then disclose the necessary work.
suggested_dialogue: The point is a repeatable handoff. The sessions are how the team builds and tests it.
branches: If the buyer asks how, show the mechanism; if they ask effort, answer directly.
practice: Translate one feature into a concrete change without promising an unverified result.
do_not_apply: Outcome language must not conceal delivery limits.

title: Use an analogy to clarify
trigger: A complex mechanism is difficult to understand.
action: Use a short original comparison, then return to the actual service.
suggested_dialogue: Think of it as a checklist at the handoff: it makes the missing step visible. The actual deliverable is [verified item].
branches: If the analogy helps, move on; if confusing, explain plainly.
practice: The buyer can state the real mechanism after the analogy.
do_not_apply: An analogy is not evidence of effectiveness.

title: Match proof to the concern
trigger: An unrelated testimonial or company statistic substitutes for answering the concern.
action: Choose verified evidence involving the relevant problem, context, and limits.
suggested_dialogue: The relevant example is [approved evidence]. Its similarity is [fact], and its limitation is [difference].
branches: If relevant evidence is absent, say so and explain what can be verified.
practice: Explain why one proof point is relevant instead of stacking status claims.
do_not_apply: Never fabricate a customer story or imply typical results from one case.

title: Keep the explanation short enough to discuss
trigger: The rep gives a long uninterrupted feature tour.
action: Explain one relevant component and check the buyer's response before continuing.
suggested_dialogue: That covers the hiring part. Does that address the issue described, or is the training gap more important?
branches: If understood, proceed; if not, clarify that part.
practice: Pause for a substantive buyer response between major components.
do_not_apply: The source's three-minute pitch is a guide, not a universal cutoff.

title: Give known factual answers
trigger: The buyer asks a concrete question about terms or delivery.
action: Answer the known fact first, then ask why it matters if useful.
suggested_dialogue: The confirmed support period is [approved term]. What needs to happen during that period for this to fit?
branches: If unknown, verify; if the requirement exceeds scope, identify the mismatch.
practice: Answer the question before returning to discovery.
do_not_apply: Do not use questions to evade refund, price, or scope information.

title: Check implementation feasibility
trigger: The offer sounds attractive but requires time or resources the buyer lacks.
action: State the actual work required and ask how it would get done.
suggested_dialogue: This requires [verified effort]. Who would own that work, and is the capacity available?
branches: If capacity exists, plan ownership; if not, consider a different option or timing.
practice: Name an implementation owner and realistic capacity before claiming fit.
do_not_apply: Do not promise effortless implementation.

title: Compare alternatives on buyer criteria
trigger: The buyer is considering another provider or doing it internally.
action: Ask which criteria matter and compare verified facts against them.
suggested_dialogue: What must the chosen option do that the current approach cannot?
branches: If the alternative fits better, acknowledge it; if uncertain, identify the information needed.
practice: Use the same criteria for all options, including doing nothing.
do_not_apply: Do not invent competitor weaknesses or claim an inevitable result.

title: Resolve contradictory service information
trigger: The buyer says a prior rep described a different offer.
action: Acknowledge the inconsistency and verify the prior statement and current scope before persuading.
suggested_dialogue: Those descriptions conflict. The team should reconcile them before asking for a decision.
branches: If current scope is verified, explain it clearly; if not, schedule only a factual clarification if wanted.
practice: Produce one consistent written scope before another buying request.
do_not_apply: A confident longer explanation does not resolve contradictory evidence.

title: Tie price to agreed scope
trigger: The rep presents a number without connecting it to the actual purchase.
action: Summarize deliverables, effort, duration, and total terms using approved facts.
suggested_dialogue: For [confirmed scope], the total is [approved amount], with [terms]. Would it help to compare the available options?
branches: If scope is wrong, correct it first; if price is the concern, diagnose it.
practice: The buyer can identify what the price covers and excludes.
do_not_apply: Check arithmetic; do not reproduce erroneous source calculations or guaranteed outcome timelines.

title: A reaction is not yet an objection
trigger: The buyer says that is expensive or pauses without rejecting the offer.
action: Allow the buyer to finish and ask what the reaction means.
suggested_dialogue: What is the main concern with that price?
branches: If value, explore expected benefit; if affordability, discuss fit and approved options.
practice: Obtain the concern before giving a rebuttal.
do_not_apply: Do not treat an absent response on a bad line as resistance.

title: Confirm the concern accurately
trigger: The rep answers a different objection from the one stated.
action: Briefly restate the concern before offering information.
suggested_dialogue: The concern is paying again without implementation support. Is that right?
branches: If confirmed, address that risk; if corrected, change the response.
practice: One accurate restatement precedes the explanation.
do_not_apply: Do not relabel a clear requirement as fear or lack of belief.

title: Find the unresolved decision
trigger: The buyer says they need to think without identifying a topic.
action: Ask what needs to become clear for a decision.
suggested_dialogue: What part needs more thought: the fit, the commitment, or something else?
branches: If specific, address it; if they want private time, respect that and offer an optional follow-up.
practice: Name the unresolved question or accept the request for time.
do_not_apply: The buyer does not owe a hidden objection.

title: Check whether the offer is wanted
trigger: The rep negotiates payment while the buyer does not see a useful solution.
action: Separate desire for the solution from its terms.
suggested_dialogue: Leaving the payment structure aside for a moment, does the actual service solve the right problem?
branches: If no, revisit fit; if yes, diagnose terms.
practice: Avoid payment negotiation before basic fit is established.
do_not_apply: A hypothetical yes is not permission to charge.

title: Separate multiple concerns
trigger: Several concerns emerge and the rep answers whichever is easiest.
action: List them briefly and ask which needs resolving first.
suggested_dialogue: There are two issues: attendance and ongoing support. Which should be settled first?
branches: If one blocks everything, handle it first; if either is a fit failure, do not stack closes.
practice: Keep a visible list of unresolved issues and mark only buyer-confirmed resolutions.
do_not_apply: Do not use isolation to demand a premature buying promise.

title: Acknowledge without invented association
trigger: The rep tries to build agreement by claiming other clients felt the same.
action: Acknowledge the concern directly; use a real approved example only if available.
suggested_dialogue: It makes sense to check who will do the work after the meeting. Here is the confirmed scope.
branches: If the buyer accepts the answer, ask the appropriate next question; otherwise clarify.
practice: No invented customer or personal experience appears in the response.
do_not_apply: The video's association step is not permission to fabricate social proof.

title: Ask permission before challenging a frame
trigger: The buyer's assumption may be incomplete but the rep becomes argumentative.
action: Ask permission to offer a factual alternative, then check it.
suggested_dialogue: Would it help to look at one other way of comparing the options?
branches: If yes, show the relevant fact; if no, stop pushing the reframe.
practice: One offered perspective followed by a buyer response.
do_not_apply: Do not shame spending choices or attack identity.

title: Check whether the answer resolved anything
trigger: The rep delivers a rebuttal and immediately starts another.
action: Ask whether the information addresses the specific concern.
suggested_dialogue: Does that answer the support question, or is something still missing?
branches: If resolved, invite the next step; if not, investigate what remains.
practice: The buyer, not the rep, confirms resolution.
do_not_apply: Do not assume silence or politeness means agreement.

title: Re-ask only after progress
trigger: The rep repeats the buying request without adding useful information.
action: Make another stage-appropriate invitation only after a concern is addressed and the buyer remains engaged.
suggested_dialogue: With that clarified, would the next meeting be useful?
branches: If ready, act; if not, identify the remaining issue or respect the decline.
practice: Each renewed ask follows a specific resolved concern.
do_not_apply: Repeated asks alone are not a coaching technique.

title: Recognize a useful no
trigger: The buyer clearly declines, opts out, or has an unmet must-have.
action: Confirm the mismatch or decision and close respectfully.
suggested_dialogue: It sounds like this does not fit the support needed. Thanks for clarifying that.
branches: If the buyer requests an alternative, discuss verified options; if not, end.
practice: Do not add a new sales loop after a clear final refusal.
do_not_apply: Not every lost sale is a rep failure.

title: Separate affordability from value
trigger: The buyer says they cannot afford it.
action: Ask whether the issue is available funds, timing, or whether the result merits the cost.
suggested_dialogue: Is the difficulty the available budget, when funds are available, or whether this is worth the price?
branches: If budget is absent, respect it; if value is unclear, revisit the problem-to-offer link.
practice: Choose one money branch using the buyer's answer.
do_not_apply: Do not assume everyone can find the money.

title: Handle genuine budget limits
trigger: The buyer confirms that the purchase is outside available resources.
action: Offer only an appropriate approved lower-scope option or a future conversation if wanted.
suggested_dialogue: Given that limit, this option may not fit. Would a smaller approved scope be useful to compare?
branches: If no suitable option, end cleanly; if one exists, explain changed scope.
practice: No recommendation to sacrifice essentials or take debt to force a sale.
do_not_apply: Motivational source analogies are not financial guidance.

title: Handle cash timing
trigger: The buyer wants the offer and identifies a concrete funding date.
action: Clarify timing and use only documented payment or follow-up options.
suggested_dialogue: When will the decision and funds be available, and would a check-in then be useful?
branches: If an approved arrangement fits, explain total terms; if not, follow up at the agreed time.
practice: Record date, purpose, and conditions rather than an assumed commitment.
do_not_apply: Do not invent a delayed charge or refundable deposit.

title: Rebuild the value explanation
trigger: The buyer cannot connect the offer to a worthwhile business change.
action: Return to the confirmed problem and explain the actual mechanism.
suggested_dialogue: The service only makes sense if [verified capability] helps with [stated bottleneck]. Is that connection clear?
branches: If unclear, explain or admit mismatch; if clear, explore the remaining concern.
practice: Use the buyer's goal instead of a generic value multiple.
do_not_apply: No guaranteed ROI or invented income increase.

title: Address a previous bad purchase
trigger: The buyer has paid for something similar that disappointed.
action: Ask what was promised, what happened, and what evidence would distinguish this offer.
suggested_dialogue: What was missing last time that would need to be different here?
branches: If the same limitation exists, disclose it; if different, show verified scope or proof.
practice: Name the actual difference and its evidence.
do_not_apply: Do not blame the buyer for not believing enough.

title: Make guarantees precise
trigger: The rep uses risk-free language or a vague guarantee.
action: State actual eligibility, conditions, remedy, exclusions, and who confirms them.
suggested_dialogue: The guarantee covers [approved remedy] under [conditions]. It does not remove the time required.
branches: If terms are unavailable, verify before claiming coverage; if excluded, say so.
practice: The replacement script contains no broader promise than the approved terms.
do_not_apply: A refund policy does not eliminate all risk.

title: Compare the cost of waiting honestly
trigger: The rep claims waiting will definitely cost a specific sum.
action: Use known current costs and disclose uncertainty about the future.
suggested_dialogue: If this continues at the current measured rate, the estimated cost is [calculation]. What might change that?
branches: If inputs are uncertain, show a range or omit the number; if reliable, compare options.
practice: Show the inputs and arithmetic behind any estimate.
do_not_apply: Do not guarantee either deterioration or improvement.

title: Present approved payment choices clearly
trigger: The rep improvises discounts or obscures the total commitment.
action: Show approved total price, installment amounts, fees, and timing side by side.
suggested_dialogue: The approved options are [A total and schedule] or [B total and schedule]. Which, if either, fits?
branches: If neither fits, stop; if one fits, confirm the full terms.
practice: The buyer can distinguish payment amount from total price.
do_not_apply: Do not relabel financing costs to hide them.

title: Downscope without pretending equivalence
trigger: A smaller offer is available for a buyer with a narrower need or budget.
action: Explain exactly what is removed and what outcome remains supported.
suggested_dialogue: This smaller option includes [scope] and excludes [scope]. Would that still solve the priority issue?
branches: If essential support is removed, do not recommend it; if sufficient, compare honestly.
practice: State one meaningful tradeoff before offering the lower price.
do_not_apply: A discount is not an automatic substitute for a fit diagnosis.

title: Turn vague fear into a checkable risk
trigger: The buyer worries the purchase will not work but cannot name why.
action: Ask which failure they are concerned about and what would reduce uncertainty.
suggested_dialogue: What is the outcome the buyer most wants to avoid here?
branches: If evidence can address it, provide it; if uncertainty remains, acknowledge it.
practice: Identify a specific risk and an appropriate evidence request.
do_not_apply: Do not describe all hesitation as irrational fear.

title: Separate calendar from capacity
trigger: The buyer says not now.
action: Ask whether the obstacle is a date conflict, time to implement, or a decision still being evaluated.
suggested_dialogue: Is the issue attending on that date, doing the work afterward, or deciding whether to proceed?
branches: If date, check approved availability; if capacity, map effort; if decision, clarify criteria.
practice: Choose the next question from the actual timing subtype.
do_not_apply: Do not dismiss all time constraints as priorities.

title: Plan around real workload
trigger: The buyer cannot assign staff or hours to implementation.
action: Clarify the actual work and available capacity before recommending a start.
suggested_dialogue: Who would own the first step, and when could they realistically do it?
branches: If no owner or capacity, defer or change scope; if available, document the plan.
practice: Identify owner and capacity without inventing a time-saving feature.
do_not_apply: Buying does not automatically create implementation time.

title: Distinguish seasonal delay
trigger: The buyer cites a busy season or major event.
action: Ask what changes afterward and whether any preparation is useful now.
suggested_dialogue: What becomes possible after that period that is not possible today?
branches: If a real change exists, plan around it; if uncertain, explore rather than accuse.
practice: Record the actual change that makes a later date useful.
do_not_apply: Do not assume waiting is avoidance.

title: Verify prerequisites
trigger: The buyer must hire, secure approval, or complete another project first.
action: Determine whether the prerequisite truly affects delivery or purchase.
suggested_dialogue: Which part of this depends on that being finished?
branches: If necessary, sequence it first; if not necessary, explain the verified independence.
practice: Draw a simple dependency before recommending a start.
do_not_apply: Do not invent urgency to bypass a real dependency.

title: Respect time to decide
trigger: The buyer needs to compare options or review terms.
action: Identify the needed information and agree a reasonable decision process.
suggested_dialogue: What information should be available before the next conversation is worthwhile?
branches: If requested, provide it; if no follow-up wanted, leave the decision with the buyer.
practice: A follow-up has a reason beyond asking again.
do_not_apply: Time for research is different from time to implement.

title: Map the other decision-maker
trigger: The buyer says a partner, spouse, or manager must be involved.
action: Clarify their role and what they need to evaluate.
suggested_dialogue: What part of the decision will they own, and what questions will they want answered?
branches: If joint decision, include them; if delegated authority, confirm the buyer's scope.
practice: Name each participant's decision role without assuming opposition.
do_not_apply: Never suggest concealing a purchase or bypassing shared authority.

title: Equip a champion without guessing
trigger: The buyer will relay the offer internally.
action: Create a factual summary of problem, scope, terms, evidence, and open questions.
suggested_dialogue: What would make this summary useful for that conversation?
branches: If they need a specialist, offer one if available; if summary suffices, keep it short.
practice: The summary contains no invented stakeholder objections.
do_not_apply: Do not make the buyer promise someone else's approval.

title: Book the stakeholder conversation
trigger: Progress requires another participant and the buyer wants to continue.
action: Agree purpose, attendees, preparation, and a feasible time.
suggested_dialogue: Would a short meeting with the implementation owner help settle the support question?
branches: If yes, propose actual available times; if no, agree an appropriate alternative.
practice: The next meeting has a decision to make and the right people present.
do_not_apply: Do not count an unaccepted invite as a confirmed meeting.

title: Handle procurement as a process
trigger: An enterprise deal needs security, legal, budget, or procurement review.
action: Map milestones, owners, evidence, and dependencies instead of forcing a one-call close.
suggested_dialogue: What must be approved, by whom, before a purchase can happen?
branches: If review is defined, support it; if unclear, find the process owner.
practice: Document the next verifiable milestone and owner.
do_not_apply: A required review is not automatically a stall.

title: Keep availability truthful
trigger: The rep claims scarcity or deadlines to overcome timing concerns.
action: Use only verified capacity, dates, and expiration terms.
suggested_dialogue: The confirmed opening is [date]. If it does not fit, the team can check later availability.
branches: If no verified deadline, omit urgency; if real, explain its basis.
practice: Every urgency statement has a current factual basis.
do_not_apply: Do not use historical course dates or fake busy calendars.

title: Ask for the next appropriate commitment
trigger: The rep gives useful information but never invites a decision.
action: Make one clear request matched to the call's purpose.
suggested_dialogue: Would it make sense to book the specialist conversation?
branches: If yes, arrange it; if concern, address that concern; if no, respect it.
practice: One unambiguous stage-appropriate ask appears.
do_not_apply: A setter does not need to ask for payment.

title: Leave room after the ask
trigger: The rep answers their own question or adds a second pitch before a response.
action: End the request and wait for the buyer's answer.
suggested_dialogue: Would the next step be useful? [wait]
branches: If they answer, follow the answer; if the line is unclear, check the connection.
practice: In practice, the rep stops speaking after the ask.
do_not_apply: Do not claim an exact original pause length without reliable audio timing.

title: Stop reselling after yes
trigger: The buyer agrees and the rep introduces new objections with extra pitch.
action: Move to the agreed action and confirm practical details.
suggested_dialogue: Great. The next action is [agreed step]. Here is what is needed to complete it.
branches: If a new concern appears, answer it; otherwise complete the action.
practice: No new benefit monologue follows an unambiguous yes.
do_not_apply: A yes to learning more is not a yes to purchase.

title: Distinguish intent from completion
trigger: The buyer says an assistant will pay later and the rep calls it closed.
action: Record the promise separately from actual payment or booking confirmation.
suggested_dialogue: The link is sent; payment is still pending. Once confirmed, the team can complete the booking.
branches: If paid is verified, mark it accordingly; if promised only, keep pending.
practice: State exactly what was observed, promised, or independently confirmed.
do_not_apply: A buyer saying good sale is not proof of collected cash.

title: Use secure purchase steps
trigger: The buyer is ready to pay and a payment workflow is needed.
action: Direct them to the business's approved secure payment channel.
suggested_dialogue: The approved secure link handles payment. No card details need to be shared in this chat.
branches: If the link fails, use approved support; if uncertain, verify the destination.
practice: No card number, security code, or identity document is requested by the coach.
do_not_apply: Do not copy source advice about collecting a card before informed agreement.

title: Book a useful follow-up
trigger: The call ends with send something or talk later.
action: Agree the purpose, participants, day, time, timezone, and preparation if the buyer wants a meeting.
suggested_dialogue: The next call would settle [open issue]. What time works with the necessary participant?
branches: If agreed, confirm invite receipt when observable; if declined, do not force it.
practice: A follow-up has a specific unresolved question and accepted time.
do_not_apply: Do not mutate a calendar or CRM without separate authorization.

title: Hand off the actual context
trigger: The buyer must explain the same problem again after buying.
action: Pass the confirmed goal, relevant facts, promises, open risks, and next owner through an authorized process.
suggested_dialogue: The delivery team should receive the confirmed goal and the commitments made on this call.
branches: If handoff is documented, preserve it; if missing, draft the summary for review.
practice: The next owner can state the buyer's goal without redoing discovery.
do_not_apply: Do not share private call data outside the authorized workflow.

title: Make onboarding concrete
trigger: A buyer says yes but does not know what happens next.
action: Explain the first action, owner, timing, and how to get help.
suggested_dialogue: Next comes [verified step] from [owner] by [confirmed timing]. If it does not arrive, use [approved contact].
branches: If timing is uncertain, verify it; if delivery has started, confirm status.
practice: The buyer knows the first action and who owns it.
do_not_apply: Do not guess preparation time or arrival dates.

title: Ask for referrals at the right moment
trigger: A satisfied customer expresses appreciation or a referral request is appropriate.
action: Ask for a permission-based introduction connected to a relevant need.
suggested_dialogue: Is there someone with a similar issue who would welcome an introduction?
branches: If yes, let the customer make or authorize it; if no, move on.
practice: A referral request is optional and does not delay delivery.
do_not_apply: Do not request private contacts without consent or imply referrals are owed.

title: Reinforce through delivery, not hype
trigger: Post-sale uncertainty appears or a team treats payment as the end.
action: Confirm expectations and make the first promised experience happen.
suggested_dialogue: The most useful reassurance now is completing the agreed first step and confirming who will help.
branches: If expectations conflict, resolve them; if aligned, follow through.
practice: Check the promised first action rather than adding more motivational pitch.
do_not_apply: Do not promise that an onboarding gesture guarantees retention.

title: Separate words from delivery
trigger: The coach attributes a weak outcome to tone from transcript alone.
action: Assess wording from text and reserve acoustic judgments for audio.
suggested_dialogue: Suggested delivery: ask the short question, then leave space for the answer.
branches: If audio exists, inspect the relevant moment; if not, label delivery unobserved.
practice: Every tone claim points to audible evidence or is labeled a future instruction.
do_not_apply: No invented confidence, sarcasm, pitch, or emotion from text.

title: Use a speakable sentence
trigger: The rep's response contains stacked clauses and abstract nouns.
action: Rewrite one thought in plain language and end with one question.
suggested_dialogue: What happens when the manager is not there?
branches: If the answer is concrete, follow it; if vague, ask for an example.
practice: Say the line aloud without losing its purpose.
do_not_apply: Shorter is useful only if material facts remain intact.

title: Ask one question at a time
trigger: The buyer answers only part of a multi-part question.
action: Split the question at the decision point.
suggested_dialogue: Who owns the training today? [wait]
branches: If ownership is clear, ask about process next; if not, explore ownership.
practice: The rep waits for one answer before asking the next question.
do_not_apply: Do not turn the call into a rigid interrogation.

title: Replace abstract impact questions
trigger: The rep repeatedly asks how it impacts the buyer after an impact was stated.
action: Use the known impact and ask the next unresolved operational question.
suggested_dialogue: Expansion depends on the top rep traveling. What would a new hire need to do independently?
branches: If the dependency is confirmed, discuss the capability gap; if corrected, revise.
practice: Each follow-up advances beyond the previous answer.
do_not_apply: Do not ask the buyer to repeat pain merely to satisfy a script slot.

title: Practice pace for comprehension
trigger: The buyer cannot follow a dense explanation and audio supports excessive speed or poor clarity.
action: Shorten the passage and rehearse with clear boundaries between ideas.
suggested_dialogue: The offer has two relevant parts. First, [part one]. [pause] Second, [part two].
branches: If comprehension improves, preserve the change; if not, revise the wording.
practice: A listener can accurately repeat the explanation after hearing it.
do_not_apply: No universal words-per-minute pass/fail threshold.

title: Use pitch and emphasis deliberately
trigger: Audio reveals unclear question boundaries or emphasis that changes meaning.
action: Model the intended question and rehearse the specific words in context.
suggested_dialogue: What would need to change for the team to handle that without the owner?
branches: If it sounds accusatory, simplify and soften; if clear, move to the next skill.
practice: Compare the original and practiced phrase for intelligibility and intended meaning.
do_not_apply: Pitch measurements alone do not establish persuasion or emotion.

title: Memorize to free attention
trigger: The rep reads rigidly and misses a buyer correction.
action: Practice the base sequence until familiar, then introduce varied buyer answers.
suggested_dialogue: That changes the picture. Let me check the revised understanding.
branches: If the rep adapts accurately, continue; if not, rehearse the listening branch.
practice: Correctly respond to three different answers without repeating a contradicted premise.
do_not_apply: Do not replace an approved live script without review.

title: Rewrite the decision, not just the adjective
trigger: A proposed script sounds smoother but makes the same wrong assumption.
action: Change the question or branch that caused the problem before polishing tone.
suggested_dialogue: The buyer already has reports. Ask what happens after the reports arrive.
branches: If the diagnosis changes, rewrite the next branch; if wording alone is unclear, tighten it.
practice: Explain which decision the new wording changes.
do_not_apply: Do not claim imitation of a trainer's voice is evidence of quality.

title: Keep quote and suggested dialogue distinct
trigger: Generated replacement language is presented as if the trainer said it.
action: Label the new line as original suggested wording; use only the verified quote bank for attribution.
suggested_dialogue: Suggested rep response: [original wording grounded in this call].
branches: If an exact verified quote fits, use it briefly; otherwise omit it.
practice: No generated script is attributed to the trainer as a quote.
do_not_apply: Do not reconstruct unpublished source passages for quotation requests.

title: Recover from losing the script
trigger: The rep loses their place and restarts discovery or rambles.
action: Return to the last confirmed milestone and identify the next missing fact.
suggested_dialogue: The goal and the obstacle are clear. The remaining question is who would implement the change.
branches: If confirmed, ask that question; if not, correct the milestone.
practice: Recover without restarting answered questions.
do_not_apply: A framework guides the conversation; it does not override the buyer's answer.

title: Choose one practice priority
trigger: A review lists many faults without a behavior to rehearse.
action: Select the most consequential supported issue and model the alternative.
suggested_dialogue: The practice target is accepting a corrected premise before the next question.
branches: If the learner can perform it, vary the buyer answer; if not, repeat this behavior.
practice: Name one visible pass criterion before the drill.
do_not_apply: A large library should produce focused feedback, not a hundred-point report.

title: Let the learner actually respond
trigger: The coach writes both sides and calls the exercise completed.
action: Present one buyer turn and wait for the learner.
suggested_dialogue: Buyer: We already receive the reports. That is not what is missing.
branches: If the learner acknowledges the correction, advance; if not, correct that one move.
practice: Practice is complete only after a real learner attempt.
do_not_apply: A written demonstration is not evidence of trained skill.

title: Correct promptly and specifically
trigger: Feedback arrives long after the rep has repeated the error.
action: Point to the exact phrase and model one change immediately.
suggested_dialogue: The next question still assumes missing reports. Try a question about execution instead.
branches: If corrected, repeat; if not, reduce the task to one sentence.
practice: The learner knows which words or choice to change.
do_not_apply: Do not attack personality or motivation.

title: Vary the buyer after repetition
trigger: The rep can recite a response but cannot adapt.
action: Rehearse the same skill with a different underlying buyer need.
suggested_dialogue: Buyer: The reports are fine; the managers disagree about who acts on them.
branches: If the rep changes the next question, pass the variant; otherwise return to diagnosis.
practice: Pass across different answers, not just identical repetition.
do_not_apply: Drill success does not establish better sales conversion.

title: Use wins and losses together
trigger: A team copies everything from a closed deal or only studies failures.
action: Compare the same behavior across comparable successful and unsuccessful calls.
suggested_dialogue: What did the rep do consistently, and what differed in the buyer's situation?
branches: If the behavior appears in both, avoid causal claims; if pattern is promising, test prospectively.
practice: Retain one counterexample for every proposed winning pattern.
do_not_apply: One sale cannot validate a catchphrase.

title: Run a useful game-tape review
trigger: A group piles criticism onto a rep without a specific next action.
action: Let the rep identify a change, preserve an evidenced strength, then rehearse one moment.
suggested_dialogue: At this timestamp, what would the rep do differently next time?
branches: If the diagnosis fits the evidence, practice; if not, replay the context.
practice: The review ends with a demonstrated behavior, not just discussion.
do_not_apply: Do not publish private recordings or employee rankings by default.

title: Train listening as well as speaking
trigger: Practice covers pitch recitation but not interpreting answers.
action: Have the learner summarize the buyer's last answer before choosing a response.
suggested_dialogue: State the buyer's problem in one sentence, then ask the next useful question.
branches: If accurate, continue; if not, replay and correct.
practice: The next question follows the actual answer, including corrections.
do_not_apply: Knowing the product script is not the same as knowing the prospect.

title: Assess readiness before live opportunities
trigger: A new rep is sent to calls based only on days employed.
action: Check accurate offer facts, recap ability, common branches, and secure next-step handling.
suggested_dialogue: The rep should demonstrate these skills on varied practice cases before owning the full call.
branches: If a critical gap remains, coach it; if ready, use supported live review.
practice: Use observed readiness criteria rather than a fixed-day guarantee.
do_not_apply: Do not recommend firing from a single call or source anecdote.

title: Separate coaching skill from closing skill
trigger: A top closer is assumed able to train everyone else.
action: Observe whether the person can diagnose, model, correct, and repeat a behavior with another rep.
suggested_dialogue: Show how a learner improves after one specific correction.
branches: If they can coach, develop that role; if not, provide a coaching process or other support.
practice: Evaluate learner improvement, not only the trainer's own sales.
do_not_apply: Do not infer management ability from charisma or revenue alone.

title: Bring delivery feedback into sales training
trigger: Reps repeat claims that delivery cannot fulfill or lose conviction from unresolved complaints.
action: Review actual customer outcomes and delivery scope with the responsible team.
suggested_dialogue: Which promises are consistently delivered, and which need correcting in the sales conversation?
branches: If a promise is unsupported, revise it; if delivery fails, fix the operational issue.
practice: One feedback loop connects sales promises to delivery evidence.
do_not_apply: Testimonials alone do not establish typical results or remove customer risk.

title: Diagnose the whole funnel
trigger: A lower close percentage is treated as proof the team deteriorated.
action: Track booked, showed, qualified, offered, purchased, and collected with explicit denominators.
suggested_dialogue: The team should compare total qualified sales and cash alongside close percentage.
branches: If volume or mix changed, analyze that change; if stable, investigate conversion behavior.
practice: Report counts and denominators for the same cohort.
do_not_apply: Do not add percentage improvements that should compound multiplicatively.

title: Compare comparable calls
trigger: A leaderboard mixes warm existing customers with cold prospects.
action: Separate stage, source, offer, buyer readiness, and rep before drawing a pattern.
suggested_dialogue: Compare these calls with others serving the same purpose and similar lead context.
branches: If comparable samples are small, state that; if sufficient, report observed patterns.
practice: Use n of N applicable calls and retain exceptions.
do_not_apply: No employee ranking from a single call.

title: Reduce unnecessary scheduling delay
trigger: An interested buyer is booked far out despite nearer availability.
action: Offer actual earlier openings without canceling the original slot until agreed.
suggested_dialogue: An earlier opening is available. Would today or the existing time work better?
branches: If earlier works, reconfirm details; if not, keep the agreed appointment.
practice: The buyer chooses the new time and understands the change.
do_not_apply: Fifteen-minute start increments do not imply fifteen-minute sales calls.

title: Make reminders relevant
trigger: Generic reminders do not reconnect the buyer with the purpose.
action: Use the agreed issue, participants, and preparation in a concise truthful reminder.
suggested_dialogue: The next conversation is about [agreed issue]. Please bring [relevant preparation].
branches: If the buyer cannot attend, offer a reschedule; if opted out, stop.
practice: A reminder contains a real reason to attend, not fake urgency.
do_not_apply: Do not make automated messages pretend to be live personal outreach.

title: Handle no-shows without inventing intent
trigger: A missed meeting is labeled disinterest or incompetence.
action: Check whether the buyer wants to reschedule and make the purpose clear.
suggested_dialogue: The meeting was missed. Would another time still be useful for [agreed issue]?
branches: If yes, agree a time; if no or opted out, stop.
practice: Record the observed no-show separately from any stated reason.
do_not_apply: Do not infer a psychological explanation from nonattendance.

title: Maintain useful call notes
trigger: Notes contain vague labels but omit commitments and corrections.
action: Capture confirmed problem, changes, objection, promises, owner, and next step.
suggested_dialogue: The note should say what was learned and what was agreed, not simply interested.
branches: If a fact was corrected, replace the premise in the summary; if uncertain, label it.
practice: Another rep can continue without contradicting the buyer.
do_not_apply: Drafting notes does not authorize a CRM write.

title: Keep follow-up purposeful
trigger: Pipeline contact repeats checking in without new relevance.
action: Use the unresolved question or agreed date as the reason for contact.
suggested_dialogue: The open question was support after delivery. The verified answer is now available.
branches: If the issue is resolved, ask the appropriate next step; if contact is declined, stop.
practice: Each follow-up references an agreed issue or useful new fact.
do_not_apply: Persistence is not permission to ignore opt-outs.

title: Inspect qualification before blaming closers
trigger: A team filters almost everyone before the close or sends clearly unsuitable leads.
action: Review actual fit criteria and downstream outcomes, not just closer convenience.
suggested_dialogue: Which rejected leads lacked a real requirement, and which were rejected before the offer was understood?
branches: If criteria are too restrictive, propose a measured test; if fit is poor, improve targeting.
practice: Use qualified throughput and outcome evidence to evaluate the change.
do_not_apply: Do not conceal material pricing to manufacture appointments.

title: Separate staffing from process bottlenecks
trigger: The team wants more hires while current capacity or conversion is unclear.
action: Measure available slots, utilized time, show rate, and actual qualified demand.
suggested_dialogue: Is the bottleneck too few available conversations, too few shows, or what happens during the call?
branches: If capacity is full, assess coverage; if not, fix the observed bottleneck.
practice: Recommend a change against a measured constraint.
do_not_apply: Do not import historical commission rates or hiring quotas as universal rules.

title: Align incentives with useful outcomes
trigger: A team optimizes easy closes, booked calls, or claimed revenue at the expense of total results.
action: Review show quality, qualification, collected cash, delivery fit, and customer outcomes together.
suggested_dialogue: The metric should reward a useful completed step, not merely a label change.
branches: If gaming is evident, redesign the measure for review; if not, do not infer misconduct.
practice: Separate booked contract, promised payment, collected cash, and later refunds.
do_not_apply: Compensation redesign needs business context; a call audit cannot prescribe it alone.
